clue.text: It enables farmers to make a good turnover

definitions.text: It enables farmers to make a good turnover

parts.words: It enables farmers to make a good turnover
parts.note: the farm implement that turns over the soil in furrows; 'turnover' pretends to be business takings

explanation.surface: A tip for farmers on how to make a healthy profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' reads as revenue, but the tool literally turns the soil over.
explanation.definitionFit: This farm implement cuts and inverts the soil, so it lets farmers turn earth over well.

clue.text: The ill cared-for neckwear found among underwear

indicators.note: the neckwear is found among the letters of the underwear, sitting inside it

parts.note: pants are underpants, British underwear
a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A sickly person's tie has somehow ended up in their underwear drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'pants' means underpants, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Those in a doctor's or hospital's care are sick people being looked after.

clue.text: Candour shown by golf tournament head

parts.note: the Open is a golf championship, as in the British Open
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: The head of a golf tournament speaks frankly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is not a leader but a promontory, a ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankness and honesty in speech are synonyms of being candid.

clue.text: Got a larger size

parts.note: sounds like buying bigger clothes, but means became bigger oneself

explanation.surface: Someone went back to the shop for the next size up.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase in size over time is the past-tense sense of the verb meaning to get bigger.

clue.text: Give voice to Beethoven's fifth

parts.note: the fifth letter of the name Beethoven is H, and to sound an H is the phonetic term asked for

explanation.surface: An instruction to sing along to Beethoven's Fifth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fifth' is not the symphony but the fifth letter of 'Beethoven', an H.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, pronouncing a sound with an audible breath of H is exactly this verb.

clue.text: One behind the scenes playing a strange game

indicators.note: the words are played about with, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A backstage worker is caught playing some odd game.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatre official who runs the backstage side of a production works out of the audience's sight.

clue.text: Lied in order to be lazy

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told a lie just so they could get out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing nothing and avoiding work are the synonym sense here: slothful, inactive.

clue.text: They're cold-blooded and calculating

definitions.meaning: venomous snakes, which are cold-blooded reptiles
things that calculate, adding machines; the adjective stands for the noun via 'They're'

explanation.surface: A description of ruthless, scheming people.
explanation.definitionFit: Vipers are snakes, reptiles with cold blood, and machines that do sums are also so named.

clue.text: Noticed liquid is deep

indicators.note: something liquid flows and changes shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spotted that a pool of liquid is deep.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is an old-fashioned synonym for having seen or spotted it.

clue.text: The stretching around three identical points produces a titter

indicators.note: the word is stretched out and its letters moved around among the added ones

parts.note: E is east, a compass point; three of the same point give three Es

explanation.surface: Someone stretching around three identical points of a shape makes onlookers giggle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small high-pitched giggle is the sound this word imitates.

clue.text: Imagined being ordered into uniform

definitions.meaning: summoned to mind, as a memory or picture is brought up

explanation.surface: A recruit dreamt they were being drafted.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory brought to mind and a conscript summoned for service both use this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Promise to present unit with weapon

parts.note: to present a gift is to give it
one is the unit number
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: A pledge made while presenting a soldier's unit with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledging, solemnly assuring someone, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Bird in danger, nesting

indicators.note: the bird is found in the letters running across these two words

explanation.surface: A bird is threatened while sitting on its nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle, a large bird of prey, is a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Located, we hear, and named

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: sited means placed or located

explanation.surface: Something was found and given a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentioned by name, as in a court list or reference, is a synonym.

clue.text: Charge made about mid-March, that's clear

indicators.note: the charge is put around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: mid means the middle letter of the word March

explanation.surface: A fee levied in mid-March is now settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unobstructed or at liberty, as a road being clear, is a synonym.

clue.text: Found sailor lying in street

indicators.note: the sailor lies inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor was discovered sprawled in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find, but is the verb to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish or set up a business is to begin it, a synonym of founding.

clue.text: It's perfectly right, for example, inside, all wrong outside

indicators.note: the example abbreviation goes inside the other letters
the jumbled word sits outside, around the example abbreviation
the word all is made wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists everything is fine within but wrong on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful and permitted, rightful in the eyes of the law, is the sense.

clue.text: Sportingly do the Highland Fling

parts.note: the Highland fling is a dance, but here it is a sporting fling at the Highland games: hurling a great pole

explanation.surface: A sporting Scot performs the traditional dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland Fling is a Scottish dance; the throw meant is the Highland games event of hurling a tree trunk end over end.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a long pole end over end is the famous Highland games event.

clue.text: It's champagne and high lights for these idols

parts.note: pop is a fizzy drink, informally champagne
stars are lights high in the sky

explanation.surface: Champagne and spotlights are the trappings of celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous singers worshipped by fans are idols of the music charts.

clue.text: It's touching when a radio entertainer gets a little money

parts.note: a DJ is a disc jockey
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: It's moving when a radio presenter finally gets paid something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' looks like 'moving', but means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Next to, sharing a border, is the physical sense of touching.

clue.text: Uncommonly tight

parts.note: tight means drunk, and uncommonly hints at a peer, someone not a commoner

explanation.surface: Something is unusually snug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommonly' is both 'very' and 'in the manner of a non-commoner', a peer of the realm.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extremely intoxicated, and a nobleman is the opposite of a commoner.

clue.text: Governor's assistant imprisoned by a revolutionary member of tribe

indicators.note: the assistant is held inside the other letters

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
a PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A governor's aide is locked up by a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people of the south-west, so one of them belongs to that tribe.

clue.text: Once you've made it, you're out

definitions.text: Once you've made it, you're out

parts.words: Once you've made it, you're out
parts.note: making it sounds like success; you are out of prison or a trap

explanation.surface: A cynical saying about success and dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking free from confinement leaves one outside, so the act is a getaway.

clue.text: No honours in such an amorous advance

definitions.meaning: an ordinary university degree without honours
a sexual approach, as in making one at someone

explanation.surface: A romantic approach that brings no credit to the suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain degree below honours level and a flirtatious move share this word.

clue.text: Growth of monastery?

indicators.note: the growth is part of, contained in, the word monastery

explanation.surface: A question about how a religious house developed.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like flower is a plant, a thing that grows.

clue.text: A unit in Salvation Army east of Suez?

indicators.note: the unit is placed in the abbreviation for the army

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army unit stationed somewhere beyond Suez.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East of Suez' was a British phrase for the Orient; the question mark marks this as a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent lying beyond the Suez Canal is the region meant by the phrase.

clue.text: One involves amusingly taking off garment right away

indicators.note: the right is sent away, removed from the garment

parts.note: a skirt is a garment

explanation.surface: Someone comically strips off a garment at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' reads as undressing but means mimicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch parodies, or takes off, its subject.

clue.text: Little intelligence

parts.note: intelligence in the sense of news or data, and little because the word wanted is a shortened form

explanation.surface: A jibe at someone not very bright.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipped informal word for facts or data, which is intelligence in the spying sense.

clue.text: He's crazy to pocket ball at end of break

indicators.note: the pocketing comes at the end of the break, after it

parts.note: to crack is to break
to pot is to pocket a ball in snooker

explanation.surface: A snooker player is mad to sink a ball at the end of a break.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person with mad ideas is the colloquial noun.

clue.text: Cause anger damaging a green

indicators.note: the words are damaged, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Damaging a golf green infuriates the club.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone furious is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Smooth flow, perhaps, late in the day

parts.note: even means smooth and level
a tide has its flow, and ebb

explanation.surface: A calm, smooth current at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the time late in the day.

clue.text: Stays in company with right clique

parts.note: a set is a social clique

explanation.surface: Someone remains with the right crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb but is the noun for stiffened supports in a bodice.
explanation.definitionFit: Old corsetry was called stays, after the boned strips that stiffen the undergarment.
